# Healing, survival and resurrection — playtest interface

**REVIEWED / reference-VALIDATED — selected scope only.** The [final notebook review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_HEALING_FINAL_CLOSURE.md) closes147 classified class passages plus6 individually reviewed ordinary spell objects. Those6 spells are now operational playtest drafts; the catalog has78 operational and770 unfinished entries. This is a bounded interface, not DD24 completion:131 additional semantic matches and healing content in other domains still need dispositions. Original cards/books are preserved.

[Exact source procedures](HEALING_DEATH_SOURCE_BINDINGS.md) · [Latest boundary decisions](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_HEALING_FINAL_BOUNDARIES.md) · [Supplement decisions](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_HEALING_SUPPLEMENT_REVIEW.md) · [Reference checks](HEALING_PLAYTEST_VALIDATION.json) · [Source integrity](HEALING_DEATH_SOURCE_VALIDATION.json)

## Distinct life operations

| Operation | Result | Restriction interface |
|---|---|---|
| Minimum-HP prevention | Preserve positiveHP instead of crossing a floor | Not HP gain; cannot create positiveHP from0 |
| Ordinary healing | Increase a living creature's normalHP | Apply modifiers, prohibitions, reserve and Critical ceiling |
| Direct state recovery | Specifically defined dying/Stable/HP recovery | Broad cannot-regain-HP applies; ordinary healing modifiers do not |
| Would-die replacement | Replace a pending death before it becomes final | Exact source eligibility; not a generic damage floor |
| Resurrection | Actually dead willing identity returns at printedHP | Separate life transition; actual corpse/soul blockers apply |
| Companion reconstruction | Restore a device/companion through its own source | No general creature resurrection permission |
| TemporaryHP | Separate nonstacking buffer | Not healing, stabilization or resurrection |

Names never select the operation. Phoenix Rebirth heals a still-living ally at0. Cleric Resurrection returns an actual dead identity. Ritual of Undeath's Ward replaces death; ordinary Death Ward is a positive-to-zero floor. Feign death and spirit manifestations are not death or resurrection.

## Damage quantities and resolution

| Quantity | Definition and use |
|---|---|
| resolvedDamage | After defenses, before tempHP; positive damage event iff greater than0 |
| tempAbsorbed | min(tempHP, resolvedDamage) |
| postTempDamage | resolvedDamage minus tempAbsorbed, uncapped by currentHP; Core Instant Death/Wounds |
| actualHpDamage | NormalHP lost to the packet after true prevention; recovery and state-assignment loss excluded |
| actualDamageDealt | NEW anti-overkill bridge: tempAbsorbed plus actualHpDamage; numeric actual-damage drains/reflections |

Ordinary “damages,” “takes damage” and “damaging hit” predicates use a positive resolved packet. Actual-HP wording (Burning Blood/Rewind Wound) uses actualHpDamage. Numeric actual-damage wording (Sanguine Rite/Echo Leech/Merciful Smite/Wound Eater/Gravebrand) uses actualDamageDealt. Source attack/hit predicates remain distinct.

Example: HP10/temp10 takes5: numeric actual damage5, actualHP damage0, positive packet. HP1 under a floor takes5: numeric0 but positive packet. HP3 takes12: numeric3, raw post-temp12. HP0 takes1: numeric0, positive packet and normal death-failure consequences.

Divine Judgment consumes its once-this-actual-target-turn entitlement on a positive packet, then reflects min(Cleric level, max(1, floor(actualDamageDealt/2))). Thus HP1-floor/numeric0 reflects1 and consumes; fully prevented resolved0 does neither. Wrathful Brand/Balanced Scales use the positive predicate where their source says damage occurred.

Resolve a damage event in this order:

1. Snapshot pre-event HP/tempHP/Wounds; resolve defenses, temp absorption and uncapped post-temp damage.
2. Core Instant Death uses postTempDamage minus preHP greater than or equal to effective maximum when reduced to0. It precedes ordinary floors. Open a legal would-die replacement; stop that packet's death procedure. No Wound save or zero-HP failure follows this branch.
3. If not Instant Death, resolve applicable true floors. They cannot raise an already0 creature. They preserve raw damage and attached conditions; a prevented drop creates no drop-only Wound trigger, but half-max/Maiming still applies.
4. Spiral-TouchedIII alone has a specific pre-Wound recovery exception. If positive-to-zero remains, spend its use, preserve that raw crossing trigger, attempt quarter-max direct recovery and apply phase-out. Broad HP-gain prohibition blocks the recovery but not the use/phase.
5. Resolve the one Core Wound save using original post-temp damage and pre-event Wounds. Fatal Wound death opens its own legal replacement window. Actual death ends Spiral phase; a successful independent Ward prevents actual death.
6. Resolve already-zero damage failures/death and its legal replacement window. A successful replacement stops skipped same-packet death branches; never replay a Wound/failure branch merely because replacement changedHP.
7. Finalize a newly surviving0 creature's dying/Stable/knockout state. Only an explicitly triggered post-zero Reaction such as Grace Reversal can act before ordinary zeroHP Reaction loss finalizes.
8. Resolve eligible post-zero Phoenix/Unyielding-style healing only if target still lives, followed by later triggers. This healing never retroactively reduces the triggering packet's numeric damage.

The affected creature chooses among simultaneously eligible offered survival effects, then rechecks remaining triggers. A paid Reaction spends its declared cost; a limited automatic survival use spends when its actual source resolves. A true floor preventing the crossing means Spiral's use is not spent. No generic extra Reaction or return from death is created.

For Ritual Ward, sufficient body and no explicitly unpreventable death are prerequisites. It can intercept Instant Death, fatal Wounds, third death-save failure, eligible direct death and lethal tracks. Positive pre-eventHP→1 is loss prevention and works through Decay. Already0 with HP gain prohibited instead becomes living Stable0: clear counters and establish a d4-hour recovery deadline immediately.

Freeze packetHpLossBeforeReplacement after true floors but before Ward. Ward metrics are min(packetHpLossBeforeReplacement, max(0, preHP minus replacementHP)); never include loss caused solely by assigning a lowerHP state. HP20 takes10 then fatal Wound/Ward1 means actualHP damage10, not19. HP5 takes100 then Ward1 means actualHP damage4, raw100.

Direct death (e.g. Wound EaterIII) produces no damage or Wound save. Its healing requires actual death; a Ward interception prevents that trigger without refunding the paid activation. False LifeI has only its printed floor and failed-death-save replacement modes sharing1/LR; it is not an all-causes Ward.

## ZeroHP permissions and start timing

A conscious but dying creature still rolls at each regular start unless Stable. Extra turns do not advance these regular-start deadlines. Further damage and actual death retain normal consequences.

Mage Undying Spellform partially overrides only zeroHP Unconscious/Incapacitated restrictions: normal speech, voluntary half-Speed movement, normal Action, legal spellcasting with that Action, and starting/maintaining concentration. No independent BA/Reaction. Existing concentration avoids automatic loss from zeroHP, but the triggering damage still requires its concentration save. Separate Stunned/Unconscious/Expedition5 or6/Silence and other restrictions still apply. Healing above0 ends the feature. Expiry at0 destabilizes, cancels the Stable recovery deadline and adds one failure; the third kills normally and permits only an eligible would-die replacement.

Oracle False LifeIII permits exactly one choice during the allowed zeroHP turn: move up to Speed, speak, or activate one Revelation. The latter uses its printed Action/BA/trigger (trigger must occur on that turn), costs and components. It can start concentration; the feature did not preserve earlier concentration. No independent actions accompany the choice.

False LifeV quarter-max direct recovery resolves at its next regular start before the death save. Blocked recovery leaves0 without invented stability; dead creatures do not revive. Spiral phase expires at its next regular start before normal start processing. Fate-BoundIV rerolls a failed death save before committing natural1/counters; use the new result. Its generic death-effect save bonus is not an ordinary death-save modifier. A natural20 whose1HP is blocked uses the previously reviewed Decay bridge: Stable0, cleared counters, immediate d4-hour deadline and preserved used-turn marker. It does not spend Ward. This differs from blocked False LifeV, which remains dying.

## Ordinary healing arithmetic

Determine legal source, recipients, costs, clocks and available entitlements before arithmetic. The helper receives already eligible modifiers; it does not acquire class powers or validate every source for its caller.

Pre-resolution modifiers include Words of Equilibrium's formula M, Zealot's Fervor +S, Throne's Grace +1/die capped S+M, Benevolent Spirits' eligible paid-technique +M, Life Prophecy maximizing dice, and Crane's applicable +S. Conditional add-ons include Ground, Radiance, Aura of Faith, Ember Mantle, Life Linked's rolled1d4, Ranger Healing Touch, Aura of Mercy, Garden's stored+1 and Tranquil Lotus Step.

First compute without conditional add-ons. Only if this preview actually restores at least1HP, recompute that same event once with its eligible add-ons. The preview changes no pools/uses. Base5 minus5 plus a conditional3 remains0; eligible pre-resolution Benevolent3 yields3. Multiple flat class bonuses use the strongest across both passes unless an explicit source exception allows stacking. Rolled extra dice/per-die changes are separate.

Within each permitted reduction plan: formula/bonuses; per-die adjustments; compatible exact fractional multipliers with one floor after multiplication; compatible flat reductions; floor at0; broad HP prohibition; maximum/Critical/reserve caps. Intrinsic Wound Eater and systemic Corrupted remain independent factors. Duplicate same-stat per-die penalties use the strongest. Dice remain dice when maximized/shared; flat Lay on Hands and stored numeric Echoes have zero healing dice.

Blight Totem cannot compound other local healing reducers. Compare systemic factors plus Totem-half alone against systemic factors plus all otherwise compatible local reducers; use the lower result. Compatible halves multiply, compatible distinct flat penalties add, duplicate same-profile groups use strongest. Suppressed reducers do not participate.

Every present, operative, applicable next-positive-healing reduction consumes exactly once when the final event commits if its pre-reduction HP potential was positive. This includes reducers whose arithmetic branch lost to Totem or whose actual gain was later blocked. Zero potential and suppressed records consume none. Two-pass preview never consumes twice.

Critical at3Wounds caps ordinary healing at max(1, effective maximum minus1); it is not a maximumHP reduction and healing cannot lower currentHP. Reserve spends only actualHP restored. A final heal8 with room3 spends3 reserve; blocked healing spends0, other activation costs remain paid. Revival/form changes/encounter starts do not replenish reserve.

## Recovery gates, triggers and loops

False Life curse gates another creature's healing SPELL: optional Insight vs RevelationDC; success permits; failed or declined check rolls d2,1 blocks HP and2 permits. Nonspell recovery and independent nonHP components remain distinct. Burning Blood blocks the cold-tagged HP-healing component only, not independent tempHP/stabilization/resurrection.

Actual positiveHP restoration is required for Radiance's cure, Renewal's Stamina, Sanctified Reprisal and Life Prophecy's RC trigger. Meditative Healing's laterKi and Transcendent Meditation's second-pulseKi are independent components and still resolve when healing caps/blocks. Blood Tithe uses its actual qualifying hostile Bleed-death trigger and finite use; not staged farming.

Passive regeneration includes Bloodthick Node, Rapid Coagulation, Regenerative Mutation and Bio-Stabilizer's modification; these retain Reserve. Finite paid/limited pulses such as Aura of Grace, Living Pulse, Renewal Totem, Blood Feast, Exsanguinate, Hemostasis, Transcendent Meditation, Cellular Reconstruction and Adrenal Floodgate are not passive regeneration. Their own Downed/Incapacitated gates remain. A passive-regeneration prohibition is not a universal healing prohibition.

Lay on Hands retains its5×Paladin-level finite pool and ordinary Long Rest refill. Base Action spends at most level on one target; Hero1/LR spends the entire remaining pool across at most3, each allocation at least1. No RP conversion. Verdict Absolute's explicit qualifying brand-kill refill is a source exception. **Remainder-conference amendment — engine[13] cadence reconciliation:** level17 Wave is1/long rest, superseding the preserved Hero card and earlier guide's1/short-rest wording. This follows the explicit engine reconciliation; the old source remains intact. Wider pool/recharge execution still belongs to the resource pass.

Transfusion donor spends K normalHP; recipient ordinary base is K+floor(K/2). Channel Life spends X; baseX. Donor must remain at least1, tempHP cannot pay, loss is not damage and cannot be prevented/redirected/refunded when recipient gets0. Recipient legal bonuses/reductions apply.

Secondary healing retains root ID and visited application IDs in a shared causal ledger, including across sibling branches. Each link/application can fire at most once/root. Numeric add-ons remain the same packet, creating no new root/child. Legal finite primary healing may trigger unrelated eligible effects.

Stronger source flags override generic provenance: Vitality Link's child blocks every further link; Echo Leech blocks secondary healing/resource triggers; Blood Feast blocks damage/resource triggers; Merciful Smite blocks Smite/heal-copy chains; Crown Undying blocks redirection/heal-copy chains; Echoes/Spiral copies retain their explicit exclusions. Source payment and direct/actual-gain predicates still apply before a child exists.

## Excess healing

OrdinaryMissingHP = effective maximum minus currentHP. Genuine excess is max(0, legal post-reduction healing minus OrdinaryMissingHP). Broad HP prohibition makes legal healing and excess0. Critical's ceiling does not redefine missingHP: max20/HP19/Critical/legalheal10 restores0 but has9 genuine excess; the missing1 is not excess. At HP20, legalheal10 has10 excess.

This quantity alone grants no conversion. A legal converter must satisfy its own costs/caps/cadences. One excess point can fund only one conversion. Source-internal Overflowing Light resolves before outside Cosmic Equilibrium uses remaining excess. Channel Life attaches a packet-wide prohibition on ALL excess-to-tempHP conversion, including another owner's feature. It permits an otherwise eligible Cosmic damage conversion.

**NEW agreed source exclusion:** Unpaid passive regeneration bounded by Mutation Recovery Reserve cannot supply excess-healing conversions unless a future source explicitly grants an exception. This covers Bloodthick Node, Rapid Coagulation, Regenerative Mutation and Bio-Stabilizer as a Bloodthick modifier. FullHP/Critical may compute mathematical excess but grants no Cosmic conversion and spends no Reserve. Do not extend this exclusion to otherwise eligible paid/finite healing merely because it restores0HP.

## Actual resurrection and retained consequences

Require an actually dead, willing identity, legal source body/anchor, location, target limit, elapsed window, paid cost and no applicable resurrection/soul blocker. ReturnedHP is a life transition, unaffected by ordinary healing multipliers or generic living HP-gain prohibitions. Explicit corpse-local and identity/soul blockers are different scopes.

Preserve Wounds/Injuries, Corruption, intrinsic Oracle Curse, debt/legal-death/body claims and spent resources. ThreeWounds is Critical, not continuous automatic death. Clear death counters/Stable deadline but preserve used turn markers and persistent histories. No duplicate creature or resource refresh.

| Class source | Exact selected procedure |
|---|---|
| Cleric Resurrection | Touch one eligible allied body, dead≤60seconds;1HP and printed2S+M tempHP1minute;3Conviction+10RP;1/LR |
| Celestial Resurgence | Up to6 eligible allied corpses30ft, dead≤18elapsedseconds;1HP;5Conviction+10RP;1/LR |
| Divine Rebirth | One successful resurrection by your Cleric feature instead max(1,floor(effectiveMax/2))HP plus printedS+M tempHP1minute;1/LR |
| Thousand Petals | At most6total including at most2eligible corpses20ft;5Ki+5RP;1/LR. Living3S d8+M healing, dead1HP. Corpse died strictly after previous source regular end. Printed floor until next source start |
| Grace Reversal | Source Reaction on surviving positive→0;10RP;one other eligible allied corpse in Oath aura since previous source regular end; Paladin stays0 |
| Soulbound Ritual / Snap Rebuild | Companion/device reconstruction via exact token/slot/expiry restrictions; no generic creature revival |

Thousand Petals revival history is campaign-persistent per Monk-owner/target identity; another Monk/source remains independent. Grace Reversal history is per Paladin-owner/target until that Paladin's qualifying Long Rest. Death of either participant resets neither. Living healing does not spend resurrection history.

Elapsed windows are inclusive (exact60seconds qualifies); previous-end windows are strictly after that typed phase20 marker through the current event. Initiative changes do not rewrite history.

## Lethal tracks after return or replacement

Both an actual resurrection and would-die replacement retain lethal tracks. Exhaustion6 becomes protected exhaustion.lethal-collapse: alive, Unconscious, no voluntary act/travel. Its static lethal endpoint is suspended for this protected return, ending once legally below6. A qualifying Long Rest can occur unconscious with another creature's care/food/water, inactive root cause and no recovery blocker.

Expedition6 retains all six provenance-bearing points and enters its existing collapse. Only genuine24hour Haven care or explicit eligible treatment can reduce it; point removal gates persist. A later positive unprevented gain at6 reevaluates either track's lethal endpoint. A fresh independently legal finite Ward may intervene; collapse is not continuing immunity.

## Removing suppressed Bleed and fire

Cures examine present, unexpired, not-ended records, including temporary suppression/acquired immunity. Initial immunity that prevented application leaves nothing to cure. Damage arbitration and active hooks still exclude suppressed/immune records.

Medicine selects one present eligible Bleed before rolling its printed/source/fallbackDC. A legal positive-potential magical heal invokes every present applicable Bleed endpoint; each Blood Curse instead receives its printedCON save. An actualHP-gain prerequisite still controls a source that expressly requires it.

A legal extinguish Action/full immersion ends all present ordinary-extinguishable fires within its scope; protected/special prerequisite fires persist. A permitted per-record fire DEX ending save remains available while suppressed when a future tick remains; no extra save after the final consumed tick. Cured records never resume when suppression ends.

## Six ordinary spells — reviewed operational playtest drafts

All retain preserved Action/RP/rank/class gates, and range120ft except Ward60ft. V/S/F uses the established M/F focus alternative; no imported material cost.

| Spell | Proposed individual operation |
|---|---|
| Stitch Fate | Rank8/21RP. Living dying0, not Stable/dead. Remove one recorded failure, or direct1HP recovery/clear counters; blocked latter becomes Stable0 with immediate d4-hour deadline. Not retrospective death undo |
| Death Ward | Rank4/7RP, concentration1minute. One positive-to-zero floor at1, then ends. No Instant Death/fatalWound/thirdfailure/lethal-track protection and no already0 recovery |
| Resurrection | Rank7/17RP. One willing identity, sufficient in-range remains, death≤8elapsedhours; return1HP and retained consequences/collapse |
| Mass Resurrection Denial | Rank8/21RP. Fixed20ft-radius sphere, concentration1minute (NEW supersedes Instantaneous). Corpse-local anchor block while remains inside; movement out/conc end/eligible rank8 removal ends block. Bodyless legal formation is not automatically blocked |
| True Resurrection | Rank9/26RP. One actually dead willing known identity, death≤7elapsed days. Usable in-range body or perceived legal unoccupied formation space120ft. Return1HP; every other remains anchor loses eligibility to duplicate that identity. No true-name or guessed soul-plane knowledge requirement |
| Soul Bind | Rank9/26RP, no concentration. Living dying0 perceived targetCHA save; failed save pending60seconds. PositiveHP/Stable ends pending. Death strictly before expiry creates bound identity for24hours from death. Exact expiry wins. One family record per identity; second legal failed save refreshes pending deadline, no post-death recast. Caster death/incapacity does not end it |

Soul Bind removal targets pending creature or existing post-death remains as local anchor. With no remains, removal must expressly free the bound identity/soul; invent no physical anchor. No mind control, ownership or indefinite prison. True Resurrection still obeys actual identity/soul barriers, and an already-living identity is ineligible. Complete objects retain countering, Dissonance/Refrain, costs and source access.

## Temporal dependency and validation boundary

Spiral-TouchedV Time Loop is temporal restoration, not generic resurrection. Its discussed participant contract restores recorded position, life/death/HP/temp/counters, Wounds/linked Injuries, Core/custom conditions, RC, per-encounter uses and snapshot Soul Bind state. Post-snapshot death/body destruction is conceptually undone; already-dead-at-snapshot remains dead. Generic corpse-resurrection denial does not automatically block it.

It does not restore RP/Ki/Conviction/BG, device resources, Mutation Reserve, daily/rest uses, physical consumables or its own spent use. The helper tests that field distinction only. Full equipment/environment topology, corpse/body-part duplication and clock rebasing remain in the dedicated temporal package; Time Loop is not declared fully operational by these tests.

Current selected checks:164 healing/death plus120 unchanged Core damage states;150 control including2 new clarification cases;98 custom including14 cure-presence cases;153 exact source records. These are interface tests, not execution of147 complete class cards, numerical balance, whole-game completion or a substitute for human playtesting.

# Enchantment control integration — provisional playtest

REVIEWED PROVISIONAL MANUSCRIPT. These NEW integration rules accompany seven approved rank-two Enchantment cards. The [exact review](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_ENCHANTMENT_RANK2_EXACT_REVIEW.md) approves the submitted body and records the binding interpretations below. Source originals remain preserved. This is not runtime certification, human balance approval, whole-game closure or GitHub delivery approval.

## Ordinary compelled Attack Actions

When an actual compulsion orders an ordinary Attack Action, use the target's native ordinary attack sequence, including inherent Extra Attack and an NPC's native Multiattack if that is actually its ordinary Action. No additional Action/attack is granted. A source expressly limited to one attack retains that limit: Confusing Flash is such an exception. An ordinary attack instruction is not permission to invent an Attack Action or convert another source's single attack into Multiattack.

Spend required ordinary ammunition normally. The command cannot activate consumable magic, special ammunition with a distinct expendable feature, RP/spellcasting, charges, recharge/per-rest abilities or optional finite-resource riders. Actual optional expenditures remain optional and cannot be compelled indirectly by choosing a method which requires them. Where instruction wording leaves the choice open, the target/controller may use a different legal ordinary method. If none satisfies the instruction, that instruction fails without spending a prohibited resource or manufacturing one. Existing source-specific limits and actual absolute prohibitions remain.

## Application IDs and independently scoped components

Each cast has a distinct application ID. Each component retains its own exact source/caster/target, application identity, deadline and actual defense state. Replacing one component never silently replaces another.

For Dire Charm, successfully established Charmed replaces only that caster's previous Dire Charm Charmed relation. Successfully established servant control replaces only the existing Dire Charm servant component across casters. Charmed-only and servant-only casts can therefore coexist. A successful repeat save, expiry or removal clears only still-active components originating from that application; an old application's save cannot remove a replacement component from another cast. Empty applications have no remaining save schedule. Core Charmed from other sources is unaffected. Shared hard-control history never refunds, even if a component is suppressed or replaced before acting.

## Compelled budget arbitration

This NEW rule resolves collisions among actual active mandatory instructions, including Command, Confusing Flash, Illusive Commands, Dire Charm and Crown of Madness. It does not create commands, extend duration, add repeated control to a one-turn source, grant new target permissions or override an explicit source-specific exception.

Record a priority timestamp for each specific instruction:
- Command, Confusing Flash and Illusive Commands: successful establishment of that failed-save instruction.
- Dire Charm and Crown of Madness: issue of that turn's particular valid order, not the age of the underlying spell alone.
- Simultaneous instructions: underlying effect application order, then a stable source/mechanical ID as the neutral tie-break. Record it before resolving choices; do not decide a favorable order after outcomes.

At execution, gather still-active mandatory instructions and consider earlier priority first. A currently impossible/ineligible instruction claims no budget; proceed to the next. Compatible requirements can share one genuine legal execution. A single Action satisfies two instructions only if that same Action actually fulfills both. Once an earlier valid instruction claims an indivisible ordinary Action/interaction, an incompatible later instruction receives no second copy. Movement uses only the actual remaining movement allowance; sequencing instructions cannot reset spent movement or violate an earlier still-maintained posture/restriction.

A losing ongoing instruction is ineffective only for its contested budget/opportunity, not automatically dispelled. Its compatible independent portions may still operate within existing permissions. Its own endpoint, replacement and saves remain. Priority loss never refunds hard-control history. An invalid later order cannot erase an earlier mandate merely by being issued.

Example: Grovel and an Attack Action may both be satisfied if Prone uses only legal movement/posture and the attack remains legal. Two incompatible ordinary Actions cannot both be demanded from one Action budget. This arbitrates actual compelled behavior; it does not make compulsion optional or restore unavailable actions.

## Six-second control cadence outside initiative

This NEW cadence binds Dire Charm and Crown of Madness's ongoing order/end-save procedures. Other sources retain their actual timing unless expressly bound by a further review.

For a target with no existing initiative/control cycle, successful outside-initiative application begins a six-second virtual target cycle: first START immediately after resolution, first END six elapsed seconds later, then repeated six-second cycles. END resolves before the next cycle's START at the same boundary. Maximum duration remains the original absolute60-second deadline; expiry can end the spell before a later opportunity.

Reviewed procedure: a target shares one active virtual control cycle and one ordinary behavior budget across concurrent control applications. A new application during an already-open virtual cycle does not replay START or replenish budgets; its specifically allowed current-cycle END save still occurs. Each spell retains its own maximum deadline, components and saves. This treats application during an outside-initiative cycle like application during an existing regular turn, preventing repeated casts from creating extra immediate Actions.

The cycle supplies the bound spells' order opportunities, one ordinary six-second behavior budget where needed, and their repeat saves. It does not refresh encounter Reactions, recharge, resources, limited uses or manufacture extra combat turns. If actual combat order becomes necessary, establish ordinary initiative before any not-yet-committed hostile behavior; a virtual cycle is no permission for an extra pre-initiative attack.

Reviewed procedure for entering initiative: map the currently open virtual cycle to the target's first actual regular turn. Carry already received order opportunities and spent ordinary Action/movement/interaction budgets into that turn; do not replay or refill them at its START. The next still-unresolved END save occurs at that actual turn's END. Thereafter use actual regular starts/ends for future triggers. Keep the original absolute duration deadline. Do not replay already resolved virtual events. Existing effects begun in initiative retain their ordinary original virtual-marker rules if they later leave it; this bridge is for these effects first established outside initiative.

Application after an actual regular START grants no order for that already-started turn. A source explicitly permitting an affected current-turn END save still grants that save. Extra turns do not add order opportunities or repeat saves.

## Fixed-zone eligibility history

Calm Emotions and Zone of Truth have fixed spherical centers and require actual exposure/line of effect from that center. Geometric presence behind total cover is not yet eligible exposure. When cover opens around a creature still inside, that moment counts as its first eligible exposure.

Keep one save/acceptance result per creature per spell application:
- Calm Emotions: willing acceptance or the actual WIS save at first eligible exposure.
- Zone of Truth: the actual CHA save at first eligible exposure.
- Success: unaffected by that cast for its remainder, including later entry/cover changes.
- Acceptance/failure: the cast's existing effect is active only while exposed inside its zone; leaving or total cover suppresses it, and restored exposure resumes it without another save.

Acceptance is not a freely toggled dispel choice. Independent zones retain separate casters, concentration, histories and deadlines. Identical restrictions or suppression do not add numerical magnitude. Being unaffected by one zone does not make a creature immune to a different cast.

Calm Emotions suppresses actual Frightened effects, including a newly acquired Frightened source. Create and retain underlying records, ordinary clocks, maintenance and scheduled repeat saves. Once no valid suppressor remains, still-existing effects resume without replaying their original application. A condition which independently expires or is cured while suppressed does not return.

No emotion-themed name automatically disables a class ability. Actual Mooncursed, Momentum Rampage, Divine Fury, Fury of the Host and Beast Empathy source cards have no new emotion-maintenance requirement here. Their real Frightened rider on an affected recipient remains subject to suppression; other printed effects continue.

## Scope and open evidence

The instruction-priority, split-component and zone histories above are authored tabletop procedures, not executed stateful engine implementations. Concurrent outside-initiative applications and the first real turn's carried budget have exact manuscript approval; executable runtime integration remains open. Human testing remains necessary for multiple-attack compulsion, long control without concentration, fear suppression and the unchanged Zone of Truth class-price discrepancy.

## Binding interpretations from the exact review

One-shot Command, Confusing Flash and Illusive Commands do not gain a new repeating cadence from this overlay. If their compelled behavior falls into the same current six-second/regular-turn opportunity, their demands compete for the same actual remaining behavior budget through Compelled Budget Arbitration.

Ordinary actual regular-start processing still happens at the first real regular turn: Reaction refresh, recharge, death-save and start effects follow their normal combat rules. Only the Enchantment control START/order opportunity and already-spent ordinary behavior budget are not replayed. The virtual START was not itself a combat turn or resource-refresh event.

For Illusive Commands, an independently valid soft movement/interaction component that survives a blocked hard Action component establishes a new instruction and replaces the prior pending same-spell record. A saved-against, wholly invalid or wholly blocked instruction establishes no replacement.

A Dire Charm application keeps its repeat saves while at least one of its original components remains. Once it has none, its save schedule stops; an old save never removes a later application's replacement component. No hard-control history is refunded.

Command's Grovel does not inherently consume the ordinary Action. Its required Prone posture can coexist with another legal Action. Confusing Flash's Attack branch continues to spend the ordinary Action on exactly one ordinary attack.

# Shared rules for the class playtest drafts

**Provisional design integration, 8 October 2026.** These rules make the class drafts usable together for testing. They preserve each protected class engine while specifying missing timing and replacing conflicting old percentages. They do not rewrite the approved Word books. Original descriptions and alternate registry entries remain in `data/playtest/class_sources`.

## Reading a class card

Use the class's own level, never total character level, for gates and effects. **L** means that class level; **S** is 1/2/3/4 at class levels 1/5/11/17. **M** means max(1, the class ability modifier), for effect a mounts only. Attacks use d20 + normal character proficiency + the actual appropriate ability modifier. Class save DC is 8 + normal proficiency + actual class ability modifier. Negative modifiers still apply to attacks and DCs. One tile is 5 ft. Fractions round down unless specified. Distances cannot be negative.

A weapon attack uses its usual ability, weapon die and damage type. A technique that says “make one weapon attack” replaces your Action with that attack; it does not also grant a normal Attack Action or Extra Attack. Generic attack-speed language has no effect beyond the exact attacks printed in the draft. A spell attack uses the class's stated casting ability. Natural 1 misses and natural 20 hits/critically doubles damage dice; flat bonuses do not double. A save succeeds at DC; “fails by 10” means the total is at least 10 below DC. Critical-range improvements never stack; use the broadest one.

An ability is known only if granted or selected by the draft schedule. Satisfy all printed prerequisites, target legality, action availability, recharge and resource costs before spending anything. A failed legal attack/save attempt still pays; an illegal activation spends nothing. No resource goes below 0 or above its cap. A class feature name shared with a spell does not grant both versions; use the version selected, with its own cost and timing. Names and source text are preserved; the current card is the operational draft.

## Action and timing limits

One regular Action, one Bonus Action if a feature permits it, normal movement and one Reaction between starts of your turns. A free trigger costs no Action only if expressly stated. All grants share **one extra full Action per creature per round**. An extra Action cannot grant another Action, recharge itself, or start another extra-Action grant. It supplies no extra Bonus Action or Reaction. A card granting additional attacks is not permission to repeat all class riders on every hit: obey each rider's frequency.

Recharge N sets a counter to N after use; reduce once at the start of the owner's regular initiative turn, whether able to act or not. Extra turns/Actions do not tick it. Outside combat tick once per 6 elapsed seconds, without double counting. Recharge 2 used on turn 1 is ready on turn 3. A positive counter can be reset/shortened at most once per ability per round. Zero counters are not legal reset targets and expend no reset use. Resets never restore RP or per-rest uses or grant an immediate activation.

An encounter is a genuine scene of uncertain opposition chosen by the Director, not a player declaration used to reset resources. No encounter gain from attacking allies, one's summons, harmless animals, helpless captives or reused corpses. Out-of-combat abilities retain all printed costs and time. Short-rest means a completed uninterrupted hour of permitted recovery; long-rest means a completed 8-hour Rest Watch. This time convention is a draft integration. Expedition pressure, supplies, safe locations and rest debt still matter. A long rest also refreshes short-rest uses; a short rest never refreshes long-rest uses. Weekly uses refresh after seven full in-world days, not repeated rests.

## Targets, concentration and control

Unless expressly stated, perceive the target, remain within range and have line of effect; total cover blocks targeting. “Ally” includes self unless it says OTHER. A list cannot contain a creature twice. Select up to the printed limit; an empty target list is not a valid way to farm activation benefits. Zones remain at their chosen point unless described as an aura; allies can leave and lose their benefits. An aura requires its owner conscious unless the card supplies a bounded exception. An effect ending at “end next turn” means the affected creature's next turn only when the card says target's; otherwise the user's.

One concentration slot for all spells, Chants, Veinweaves, forms or zones that require concentration. Starting another ends the old before the new effect resolves, except for an explicit limited linked-effect rule. Damage prompts CON save against max(10, floor(damage/2)); incapacitation or a failed save ends concentration. The round-down convention is a deliberate pilot interpretation. Concentration does not demand a Bonus Action unless maintenance says so. For a paid 3-pulse effect, start is pulse 1; pay maintenance on each of the next 2 regular turns by turn end for pulses 2/3. Missing payment ends it at that turn's end; otherwise it ends at start of turn 4. No repeated start triggers on maintenance.

Forced movement does not provoke opportunity attacks unless explicitly stated, cannot place a creature inside solid matter, and stops at an obstacle. Grapples use the card's save/DC, can be escaped with an Action and STR(Athletics) or DEX(Acrobatics) against that DC, and end beyond reach. A root sets Speed 0 but does not remove Actions. Slows reduce Speed to minimum 0. Silence blocks verbal spells/audible abilities, not all thought or all class features. Charmed effects never determine a player's beliefs; use only the printed action restrictions.

No repeated hard denial without a new save and cost. For this class suite, a creature can suffer **Stunned, compelled loss of its whole Action/turn, or equivalent hard denial from a given character at most once per encounter**, across that character's class features; later such riders fail while damage and soft riders resolve normally. Record source and target. This draft guard is broader than the older Oracle-only ceiling and is an explicit balance proposal. Reaction denial, Speed reduction, penalties and Frightened do not count as whole-turn loss. Do not silently waive boss immunities, legendary defenses or anatomy.

## Damage, healing, stacking and companions

Roll once for each shared area/pulse and apply saves/defenses to each target separately; separate attacks roll separately. Halve once for a successful save and apply resistance/immunity normally. Same-named conditions/bonuses do not stack unless a printed cap allows it; same-stat flat bonuses from these class techniques use the strongest. Different resources remain separate. Damage reduction from these class features uses the strongest flat reduction, then applies resistance; it cannot create negative damage or healing. Temporary HP never stack; choose the larger remaining amount. Immunity is not reduced resistance.

Repeated permanent HP recovery must consume finite RP, a per-rest use or another finite resource; a combat-generated gauge alone never enables unlimited healing. Healing cannot exceed maximum HP or erase Wounds, death consequences, debt or Corruption unless explicit. Downed is living at 0 HP; dead is different. Resurrection requires a willing soul and sufficiently intact body, obeys its time window, cannot create a duplicate and never refunds the feature on failure to meet known prerequisites. Sacrificial HP is actual unpreventable loss, cannot be redirected or paid with temporary HP, and is not damage for resource triggers. It cannot reduce the donor below 1 unless a card expressly grants a death-triggered effect.

No damage/healing copy repeats the source's costs, procs, resource generation, critical bonus dice, buffs, actions, cooldown resets or duration. Compute fractions once, capped at 100% of one stored source unless an explicit card states a separately priced higher amount. Copies still cause ordinary damage consequences, concentration checks and death. A copy cannot copy another copy. A target/source record must refer to an actual resolved event, not merely a known ability name.

Where a class card calls for a **standard companion** without a more specific profile, use: Small or Medium; AC 12+floor(PB/2); HP 2 L; walking Speed 30 ft; saves equal owner's PB; one melee or ranged attack (reach 5 ft/range 30 ft) at owner's class attack bonus, damage S d6 of the printed type. It has no independent class features, resources, loot, death triggers or extra turns. All companions belonging to one character share one Bonus Action command and **one damaging attack/action total per round** unless a specifically priced feature grants more. Without a command they move and Dodge. Act immediately after owner. A standard companion lasts 1 minute, disappears at 0 HP and cannot be healed for free by dismissing/resummoning. The creation cost must be paid again. Creature-specific stat blocks override this profile only where explicitly printed.

## Ordinary spells: one explicit test configuration

Use the manifest-owned **Core Systems Known Descent V 2** class RP tables and rank costs: rank 0–9 costs 0/2/3/5/7/10/13/17/21/26; Grand 32. Follow `src/data/class-spell-progression.js` for each class's rank gates and the existing spell catalog for class/school access. Having enough RP never bypasses a rank gate. Oracle has Revelation Charges, and Soldier/Warrior have no general RP spellcasting. Multiclass spell access is determined separately per class; do not add complete class pools or use total level to unlock a rank. This suite's printed pool tables are single-class; use the existing multiclass pool formula with the new constituent Core V 2 pools for mixed characters.

Four classes have no direct Core V 2 pool row. For this pilot, Crimson Agent uses the Cleric curve multiplied by 0.5; Dragoon, Monk and Thief use that curve multiplied by 0.35, rounded to nearest integer with halves upward, minimum 1. These fallback factors come from the preserved `src/data/resonance-economy.js`; they are explicitly distinguished from direct book tables. The generic Core V 2 Oracle RP row is rejected for this class suite because Oracle's protected class contract uses Revelation Charges only. Oracle never receives RP or ordinary spell access. Retune here means one recovery at the end of a completed short rest, not an unrestricted action.

For a reproducible pilot, retain the protected **Dissonance** layer with Core V 2 numeric RP costs. This combination is a new integration decision: do not also roll a second historical Burn/fizzle system on top of it. Limit=max(4, 2+PB+max(0, casting modifier)). Before a ranked cast, Dissonance at limit/limit+3/limit+6 adds 1/2/3 RP respectively; at limit+6 ordinary casters cannot cast rank 1+. At limit+3 ordinary Overcast is unavailable. A cast then adds base Dissonance 0 at rank 0, 1 at ranks 1–5, 2 at ranks 6–9. Immediate repeated casts of the same named spell add 1, 2, then 3 maximum. Another named spell resets the repeat counter but not accumulated strain. Apply the class's exact cadence reduction/vent; never infer a free RP reduction. Printed class techniques pay printed costs and cause no automatic spell Dissonance unless tagged or expressly described as spells, Echo releases or Matrix casts. For a Mage/Wizard class card tagged as a spell, use the rank printed in normalized data; its rank is fixed at acquisition and does not rise with S. Other techniques are not counterspell able unless their card says so.

Retune recovers max(0, round(max RP/4)+casting modifier), never above maximum, and clears Dissonance. A long rest restores RP and clears Dissonance. Optional 10-minute meditation once/day recovers positive casting modifier RP and reduces Dissonance by PB+positive modifier. A regular turn with no spell or magical class ability loses 1 Dissonance; an Action spent Grounding without casting loses PB instead (not both). Merely ending an encounter does not clear accumulated Dissonance. Refrain survives idle/weapon turns unless a class explicitly clears it. Lich/Necromancer may force ranked casts through Fracture; after resolution take direct unpreventable trauma equal to rank×1/2/3 at the three strained states, minimum 1, based on state before casting. This trauma cannot generate resources or trigger damage-sharing. They still pay RP and meet rank gates.

Generic Overcast is excluded from the initial suite configuration until its options are separately fixed; cards such as Overchannel have their own exact costs and gates. Core V 2's original Burn procedures, older rank×2 costs and smaller companion RP tables remain preserved as alternatives, not silently combined. This configuration is suit able for comparing class drafts, not a claim that all historical magic sources already agree.

## Spell repertoires and acquisition

Preserve explicit class spellbook/preparation rules where given. For classes missing a known-spell count, this suite proposes: full casters know 3 cantrips at 1, 4 at 4, 5 at 10 and choose 2 ranked spells at first spell access plus 1 each later class level; hybrid/half/minor casters know 2 cantrips at first cantrip access and 3 at class 10, and choose 2 ranked spells at first ranked access plus 1 on each later even class level. At a long rest, a known caster may replace one known spell with a legal same-or-lower rank selection. This fills an actual missing rule and does not replace a more specific Druid prepared list or Wizard spellbook. Bonus spells expressly granted by a class are additional. No unnamed or mechanically unfinished catalog spell becomes complete merely by entering this repertoire; select operational spells for the test and record them.

Scheduled selection applies only where the class document says so. At each milestone choose distinct eligible entries; no banked Skill Points. Automatic engines, ASIs, feats, forms and finales do not also consume a choice unless stated. Ordinary-class schedule:4 Base at 1 (at least 2 active), 2 Base at 2; 2 Arch at 3 (at least 1 active); alternating 1 Base/Arch at 4/6/8/11/13/15/17/19 and 1 Arch at 5/7/9; choose Hero at 10 and 2 Hero (at least 1 active), then 1 Hero at 12/14/16/18; finale 20. If a class has no source Arch capstone, level 9 has the printed class-specific grant or another choice, explicitly shown. The individual schedule and prerequisite checks win over this summary. ASI or eligible feat at 4/8/12/16/19, separate from choices, except Oracle uses its explicit 4/8/14/19 schedule. Druid, Oracle and Paladin use their own schedules.

## Source and review status

The owner asked to extend the Bard treatment to all classes. Each draft separates the original wording, provisional numerical specification, acquisition and examples. Earlier contradictory level-table entries are retained as source evidence and marked reconciled/replaced for this draft; never stack them on top of the new schedule. Automated checks cover acquisition, source completeness and selected resource invariants. Human table play is still needed to judge balance, fun, and numerical tuning.


## Core condition reference

The following descriptions are preserved from [Core Systems Known Descent V2](../../data/public/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Data_v2_Known_Descent.json). The class suite adds its explicit duration, escape and hard-denial limits; it does not give the same named condition a different meaning in each class. Dread, Grief, Bleed and other custom riders use their card’s exact definition.

# Maximum HP, stat changes and HP thresholds

**REVIEWED / reference-VALIDATED —58 exact passages:51 class records and7 feats.** The [source register](MAXIMUM_HP_SOURCE_BINDINGS.md) preserves the original procedures; [source validation](MAXIMUM_HP_SOURCE_VALIDATION.json) verifies equality and hashes. The [first captured notebook reply](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_MAXIMUM_HP_FIRST_REVIEW_PARTIAL.md) is incomplete and must be read with the [complete tail and boundary corrections](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_MAXIMUM_HP_BOUNDARIES.md) and [exact implementation closure](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_MAXIMUM_HP_FINAL_CLOSURE.md).

These rules cover the maximum-HP and threshold components supplied here. They do not promote whole feats, create companion actions, decide character advancement, or certify every monster/item/spell maximum-HP modifier.

## Recompute capacity from separate records

Keep base maximum, bonuses, reductions and systemic multipliers separate. Base maximum excludes all modifiers represented separately in this ledger. Never feed a previously modified maximum back into the formula.

First calculate the otherwise-applicable maximum:

    preSystemicMaximum = max(1, baseMaximum + compatibleBonuses − strongestMonkTrauma)

Then apply the reviewed systemic factors against that same value:

    effectiveMaximum = max(1, floor(preSystemicMaximum × systemicFactors))

Expedition Strain4+ contributes3/4 and Exhaustion4+ contributes1/2. Multiply compatible rational factors before rounding once. Base101, Flesh Warden+20, Monk trauma−9 and both factors produce42. Suppressing that trauma produces45; do not subtract the trauma again afterward.

The numerical modifier calculation does not perform lethal-track transitions. Use the separate reviewed life-state procedure when a track actually changes. Merely recomputing maximum HP must not re-kill a living collapsed survivor at track6.

Each application retains its own ID, source, owner, target, magnitude, start/end markers, presence and suppression state, arbitration group and any acquisition/creation snapshot needed for its formula. Keep records even when another stronger application wins. Suppression does not stop clocks.

## Bonuses and source identities

| Source | Bonus and update rule |

| Flesh Warden | +2 per Warrior level while legally equipped; capacity only |
| Wizard Conjuration specialization | +Wizard level captured when that Wizard spell creates the summon |
| Flesh Ascendant | +2 per current Wizard level of the eligible controller supplying the feature |
| Familiar Bond | Provisional +current eligible owner's character level to familiar maximum HP |
| Tenacity | +current character level |
| Tough | +twice character level when the feat was acquired; retain this snapshot |
| Tough as Nails | +2 per character level at acquisition, then +2 for each later level |
| Dark Fortitude | +2 per current character level |

**New feat integration:** distinct feat identities granting maximum HP add together unless an explicit source says otherwise. Duplicate copies of the same feat do not add. Their original acquisition/prerequisite, retraining and other-effect rules still need their separate review.

**New Wizard-specific stacking exception:** Conjuration and Flesh Ascendant add when the same undead summon qualifies for both, overriding the frozen strongest same-stat class-technique bonus default for this pair only. Flesh Ascendant's engine[24] and named card describe one modifier identity; do not count both.

When later companion lifecycle code constructs records, the engine/card aliases must share one actual effect identity, including suppression and removal. Numerical non-stacking alone must not leave a second textual alias operative after that effect is suppressed.

Conjuration's amount and caster provenance stay tied to creation. A later caster level or controller change does not recompute that snapshot. Flesh Ascendant instead follows the current eligible controller; changing control ends the old controller's eligibility and can create the new controller's eligible bonus, without healing.

Initial creation under that bonus can include it in starting HP; later level increases add capacity only. Base20 plus Conjuration10 plus Flesh Ascendant20 gives50/50 at creation. Acquiring either bonus later does not fill missing HP. No bonus changes creature or command caps.

## Monk trauma uses one global strongest reduction

**Explicit correction of the earlier per-owner proposal:** Monk engine[9]'s categorical non-stacking clause controls. Use the largest currently operative Monk maximum-HP reduction on the target across all owners.

Ribcrusher applies S+M, Bone-Breaking Strike2S+M, and Deathless Silence4S+M. Preserve each successful application separately, including repeated applications of the same card. Do not combine the strongest magnitude with another record's longer duration. If−9 is suppressed, an operative−5 can become effective; when−5 expires, it stops contributing even while−9 remains suppressed.

Default Monk trauma ends when the target completes a short or long rest. This is effect removal, independent of how many numerical rest rewards the target already earned. Interrupted rest ends none. A genuinely explicit earlier/different endpoint controls its own record; the existence of an endpoint parameter does not grant permission to invent one.

Deathless Silence has three independent components: the Monk's protection from Reactions/opportunity attacks through source-next-regular-start; target defensive-passive suppression through that target's next-turn end; and maximum-HP trauma through the target's completed rest. Preserve the already reviewed control clocks.

## Capacity changes are not HP damage or healing

After any maximum change, clamp current normal HP down only if it exceeds the new maximum. Adding/restoring maximum HP gives no current HP. This clamp is not damage, sacrifice or healing; it creates no Wound save, death-save failure, resource trigger, redirection or first-fall event. Decay does not prevent capacity restoration.

Temporary HP is independent and remains unchanged. Maximum reduced to10 does not remove an existing25 temporary HP.

Dead, Stable and dying0 creatures retain their life state, counters and Stable deadline. A minimum maximum of1 never revives a corpse. Critical's healing ceiling recomputes afterward as max(1,effectiveMaximum−1); it is not another maximum-HP reduction.

## Exact thresholds and recorded events

Use effective maximum and integer comparison, without rounding a percentage threshold first:

| Wording | Comparison |
|---|---|
| At/below one-quarter | 4×HP ≤ maximum |
| Below one-quarter | 4×HP < maximum |
| At/below half | 2×HP ≤ maximum |
| Below half | 2×HP < maximum |
| Above half | 2×HP > maximum |

Continuous predicates update whenever HP or maximum changes: Wyrmhide, Brutality Sense, Pain Empowerment, Dark Fortitude's poison resistance, Life Drinker's conditional damage, and “below maximum” regeneration eligibility. Pain Empowerment uses full10% missing-HP bands, capped at+5, at its printed pre-roll moment.

**New first-fall interpretation:** Anointed Guardian, Burning Blood IV, Death's Threshold and Adrenal Floodgate require a genuine downward crossing. At/below-quarter triggers require HP moving from above quarter to at/below quarter. Burning Blood IV requires moving from at/above half to strictly below half. Actual damage or direct HP loss can establish a crossing unless a source specifically restricts it to damage. Capacity changes and clamps cannot.

If a rest refreshes a first-fall use while its subject is already below the threshold, neither the refresh nor another1HP loss fires it. The subject must return to the non-trigger side and cross again. Source frequency/history remains a separate eligibility gate; a crossing alone grants no new use.

Death's Threshold's exit requires actual HP restoration leaving the creature above half. A maximum reduction that makes unchanged HP above half does not end it. A later actual heal can satisfy that exit even if the creature was already above half before that heal.

**New continuous duration interpretation:** Mythic Carapace and Butcherform Chassis end when active and strictly below quarter. A maximum increase can therefore end them without damage. Exact quarter remains legal. Other duration endpoints still apply.

Record pre/post normal HP and the event-effective maximum for historical checks. Rewind Wound uses the maximum stored with its referenced damage event, never a later maximum. Freeze same-event HP crossings before a later stat clamp.

Rewind Wound requires genuine damage causing actual normal-HP decrease and leaving the target below half; it does not require a first crossing. HP40→30 at maximum100 qualifies even though both values are below half. An event entirely absorbed by temporary HP does not qualify.

Selection/rider timing follows each card: Mass Healing Light when its target is chosen; Merciful Sacrament at initial activation; Flesh to Ash before rolling damage; Death Touch at strike start; Blessing of the Meek/ Verdant Pulse before healing; Final Verdict at legal targeting; Fearbrand/Malicious Execution before their damage/rider; Echo Strike after its copied damage. Brutality Progress's already reviewed snapshot rules remain unchanged.

## Percentage recovery and damage

Use effective maximum when the amount resolves unless the source explicitly references an earlier snapshot. Floor the percentage amount, with minimum1 only where printed or already supplied by the reviewed viable-resurrection bridge.

Wound Eater III can heal0 at maximum3. Spiral III and False Life V explicitly retain minimum1 for quarter recovery. Unyielding Light uses one third with minimum1. Divine Rebirth uses the reviewed viable-return max(1,floor(maximum/2)). Wound Eater V's quarter target-HP loss and half self-heal cap retain their direct-loss classification. Ledger Unbound caps its raw damage at a quarter of target maximum before its save-halving.

Repair Pulse and Snap Rebuild use half device maximum under their own functional/destroyed target rules. A tiny-maximum reconstruction's viability belongs to the device lifecycle and is not silently converted into a general minimum1 here.

## Attack damage before Monk trauma

**New integration for the supplied Monk trauma cards:** choose/pay an after-hit option at its legal hit window. Resolve the ordinary attack's damage, Wounds, Instant Death and any survival replacement against the pre-trauma maximum; freeze its metrics. If the target remains an eligible living creature, resolve the trauma CON save using its then-current save modifier, including applicable Wound consequences. On failure, create the trauma record and recompute capacity.

If the attack leaves the target Dead, no combat-trauma record is needed and the paid cost is not refunded. A legal same-resolution death replacement preserving life can leave the target eligible.

Example: maximum30, HP30; damage4 leaves26 and records4 actual damage. A later−15 maximum reduction gives maximum15 and clamps current HP26→15. The11-point clamp causes no second damage/Wound/threshold event and cannot rewrite the attack's Instant Death threshold or concentration packet.

## Validation and remaining scope

The current reference passes60 targeted checks and909 systemic parity states. It accepts already legal source records and event snapshots; it does not decide source acquisition, perform companion creation, pay Ki, schedule turns or consume first-fall uses.

Still open: unsupplied item/spell/monster/disease/curse maximum modifiers; non-Monk reductions; exceptions applying after systemic multipliers; full feat acquisition/retraining; familiar and summon/control lifecycle; unusual device reconstruction; human balance. Missing inputs mean *unvalued*, not zero or infinite price. No ordinary sword or crafted Masterwork acquires artifact multipliers by being recovered from the dungeon. Record gross and each deduction separately. A negative net estimate exposes a possible liability; it is not a compulsory purchase, debt or negative payment to a seller. ### FL-21 — One settlement ledger Keep exact fractions of copper until each actual final payment. Use 1 sp = 10 cp, 1 gp = 100 cp and 1 pp = 1,000 cp. Where accepted, retain 1 Mithril Mark = 500 cp, Embermark = 2 sp, Soulshard = 1 gp and Tidesilver = 1 sp. For each entry, record transaction ID, payer/payee, currency, goods/quantity or service, agreement/authority, exact quote, actual rounded payment, timestamp, status and related prior payment. Quoted, reserved, paid, owed, refunded and lawfully written off are different states. A price quote spends nothing. Apply deposits to their agreed bill. Insurance is an inflow, not sold cargo. For the default Loop net-share sponsor agreement: `SponsorBase = max(0, G − T − RQ)` `SponsorShare = contracted percentage × SponsorBase, rounded once as payment` `NetExpedition = G − T − RQ − SponsorShare` G is actual sale receipts, T the direct Haven taxes on them, and RQ the episode's actual mandatory rescue/quarantine expenses. Count RQ once whether paid earlier or now. This sponsor base is before personal wages and discretionary purchases. A signed gross-share or priority-lien agreement instead uses its own declared terms. True profit includes actual episode inflows less every distinct actual episode cost once: shares, wages, consumed/replaced supplies, operating fuel, repair, interest and other agreed costs. Show capital purchases and borrowed principal separately. Loans and principal repayment are financing, and selling existing personal capital is not earned cargo. Cash allocated to next-expedition reserves is a further allocation, not automatically the same as profit. Report the charter's gross cargo target, net expedition target and true-profit/distributable-after-reserves target, stating whether the comparison is an appraisal or a realized sale. Appraised value does not pay wages. Keep insufficiently funded obligations owed; do not invent negative inventory, a compulsory new loan or unlimited sponsor funds. Allocations cannot exceed actual available money. ### FL-22 — Claims, sponsors, taxes and insurance Record entitlement and permitted disposition before spending or selling. The Core priority is actual authorized emergency survival use; existing liens/charter claims; wages, porter shares and rescue costs; Gate/sovereign taxes and authorized seizure; written party division; then sale, donation, study, crafting or retirement. A title dispute or incompatible orders needs a real hearing. Priority neither waives a due sale tax nor charges a bill twice. Use the **single highest applicable** Loop levy on the same taxable disposition: | Actual transaction category | Levy | |---|---:| | Registered routine goods | 3% | | Licensed crafting materials/goods | 5% | | Artifact auction | 6% | | Strategic/regulated cargo | 8% | | Authorized contraband-amnesty disposal | 12% | Identify category and jurisdiction before the offer. Ordinary purchases do not acquire this sale levy; separate tolls, hearings or seizures need their actual authority/contract. The provenance rate r is 60% undocumented, 75% disputed or 90% documented/Gate-Sealed. This new partial-loss calculation matches the source whole-loss formula when L = I. A later claim does not restart the deductible or pay the full total again. Give an actual safe-access claim notice within 72 elapsed hours of return; an earlier authenticated notice counts. Declared inability to communicate postpones the deadline until communication is restored, without backdating coverage. Routine examination needs two active hours of qualified work plus real evidence-gathering time. It is not guaranteed payment in two hours. Fraud, undeclared cargo, voluntary abandonment without a prior insured-sacrifice clause, and loss after knowingly ignoring an applicable abort condition are excluded. Insurance supplies money under terms, never new material, HP, souls or a restored person. ### FL-23 — Standing and earned history The new ordinary policy, **standing-v1**, uses an integer from −3 to +3 for each resolved individual/institution relationship: | Score | Description | Ordinary access guide | |---:|---|---| | −3 or −2 | Hated | An actual willing provider, safe intermediary or specific exception; no automatic attack | | −1 | Disliked | The provider's ordinary public dealings under its real restrictions | | 0 | Neutral | Eligibility to ask for public goods, lodging and contracts | | +1 | Liked | Consideration for an offered introduction/license/buyer process | | +2 or +3 | Honored | Consideration for offered bonded storage, credit, sensitive desks or senior audiences | These are opportunities to seek actual services, not granted offices, ownership, credit balances, licenses, waivers or auction admission. Named existing entitlements keep their own terms. Hated with one institution does not ban unrelated public services. Keep +2 and +3 distinct even though both display Honored; absence, unresolved information and hidden data are not an explicit known Neutral 0. Reputation as a CHA skill is a separate applicable check: add proficiency once, not proficiency plus the relationship score. The actual known-buyer mundane sale fraction remains its specific equipment rule. A significant public attributable ordinary event can propose ±1; a major public success/betrayal ±2. Within one subject/institution/scene, add the signed proposals, cap their sum at −2…+2, then apply it to that scene's opening score and clamp the result to −3…+3. No banked overflow or extra award per witness/report. A campaign-defining exception requires its real distinct event and expressly predeclared magnitude/cap exception. Other institutions respond only to information actually reaching them and their own stakes. NPC attitude, Expedition renown, legal status and named privileges remain separate. For a genuinely fresh Cult Escapee, bind the full background to actual institutions: former cult Hated/−2, suspicious religious authority Disliked/−1, anti-cult group Liked/+1. This does not target every cult or religious order. Existing earned history is never overwritten by a fresh-start value. ### FL-24 — Haven work, services, learning and recovery A Haven Turn is **24 elapsed hours**, not a token that buys any result. The provider supplies compatible real inputs and the exact method/lot limits: use 30 minutes per lot and the 24-hour treatment where that is the governing method. Payment cannot preserve an unsupported active core. Ordinary repair service takes the actual qualifications and at least max(1 hour, maximum HP/10 hours); special Broken magic bodies retain their specific requirements. An inclusive service price replaces the self-repair material bill. ### FL-25 — Coins, unlawful operations, labor and rescue Track each coin's denomination, composition, count/weight, custody and actual mint acceptance. Declare the assay method and suspected defect before the roll; do not make a generic and specific test for the same uncertainty or switch to the easier one after failure. | Generic bulk assay | DC | |---|---:| | Obvious defect | 10 | | Mixed/clipped coin | 13 | | Plated/adulterated coin | 16 | | Expert false mint | 19 | | Specific Core method/defect | DC | Preserved value range | |---|---:|---| | Trace shaving, 1–3% | 12 | 95–99% face | | Light shaving, 4–8% | 14 | 85–95% face | | Heavy shaving, 9–15% | 16 | 70–85% face | | Ruined shaving, 16–30%, once weighed | 10 | 40–70% face | | Washed/plated, without cutting or magic | 18 | 5–25% recoverable value | One ordinary assay work unit handles up to 100 coins or 10 lb, whichever limit is reached first, in 30 active minutes. Keep materially different variants identified. Use INT (Investigation) or the relevant actual proficient tool once. An applicable functioning jeweler's-scale, touchstone, milled-edge or merchant-test-kit method can supply its source proficiency contribution to that assay, not a second proficiency bonus, general training or supernatural detection. Destructive testing spends the actual sample. Routine documented weighing needs no new roll. Failure leaves uncertainty. Only a declared false-assessment stake can give a fallible critical-failure report; no die changes metal. New evidence or a genuinely different test can justify more work and another roll. Changing the appraiser alone cannot. A combined commissioned assay bill receives its minimum once, not per coin, variant or thirty-minute stage; services not incurred create no fee, and an already-owned private testing toolkit creates no fictional desk fee to its owner. NEW explicit total-payment and fee allocation: let F be the confirmed false lot's face value, A the actual assay fee, R the actual remint fee, and S=A+R for the same assessed lot/bill; the total monetary liability is P=max(0.10×F,S), allocated to service fees S and an additional criminal fine of P−S=max(0,0.10×F−S).
